constants.documentedValue: 1.7 (= lightMapIntensity)
constants.measuredValue: EXP itself is 1.7 (bake.js:66), but the property the row names, mesh.material.lightMapIntensity, is actually set to 1.7 * Math.PI ~= 5.3407 (bake.js:498), not literally 1.7
constants.howMeasured: tour/bake.js:66 `const EXP = 1.7;`; tour/bake.js:498 `mesh.material.lightMapIntensity = 1.7 * Math.PI;`
constants.notes: Not a functional bug -- bake.js:481-497's own comment explains the *Math.PI is deliberate, cancelling r185's shader-side *RECIPROCAL_PI so the delivered contribution still equals EXP=1.7, matching r128. But the CLAUDE.md row's parenthetical '(= lightMapIntensity)' reads as the property equalling 1.7, and it does not -- the property is EXP*PI. A documentation-precision finding, not a rendering defect. Lineage, verified directly rather than assumed: `git show fad9ada:tour/bake.js` (pre-r185-migration) had `mesh.material.lightMapIntensity = 1.7;` literally (line 169 of that blob) -- so CLAUDE.md's '(= lightMapIntensity)' WAS true at the time it was presumably written. The r128->r185 migration commit `67e5582` ('Close the r128<->r185 lighting/colour gap...') changed it to `1.7 * Math.PI` (its own commit message: 'tour/bake.js: lightMapIntensity 1.7 -> 1.7*PI. r185's MeshBasicMaterial lightmap shader chunk gained a `* RECIPROCAL_PI` r128 never had...') and did not touch CLAUDE.md in the same change. The row went stale at that specific commit, not gradually.

constants.notes: Set to null, not false: this row's absolute figures and their ratios are a class CLAUDE.md rule 4a itself declares NOT comparable across machines/sessions ('the three sets are not comparable: they were taken on three different machines'), so `agrees: false` would assert 'the documented figure is wrong' about a figure the rule says has no single right answer -- and would invite a later task to edit CLAUDE.md's bake row into a rule-4a violation by chasing this session's number. Recorded, not corrected. Basis for that null, made explicit: (1) rule 4a already records an 11301-21768 ms spread across THREE LOADS OF AN IDENTICAL BUILD on kings-court -- a ~2x same-build spread on one machine. This session's kings-court median, 22294.2 ms, sits at or above the TOP of that already-known band, so part of the apparent divergence is inside a spread CLAUDE.md already documents, not new. (2) serenity measured 834.4 ms this session against a documented 2620 ms -- roughly 3x FASTER, the OPPOSITE direction from kings-court's ~2x-8x SLOWER reading. A single explanation such as 'this machine/session is more loaded' cannot produce both a apartment running faster and another running slower than the documented reference at the same time; that inconsistency is recorded here, not resolved. (3) This session ran three page loads per apartment with no machine identity recorded, no cold/warm distinction, and the three apartments were not served against a common reference build in the same batch (unlike, e.g., plan 3's closing-gate method of serving BASE and HEAD simultaneously). Given (1)-(3), the ~26.7x kings-court/serenity and ~3.18x horkyone-10/serenity cross-apartment ratios computed from these numbers are directionally interesting -- this session's spread between apartments is wide -- but are NOT a supportable ratio claim in the sense rule 4a means when it says 'compare ratios within one machine's before/after pair and nothing else': this session has no before/after pair, only one snapshot on an unidentified machine. Whether browser-tab contention, server load, or genuine hardware variance explains any of it is unestablished and out of this task's scope.

constants.constant: Two-camera FOV finding: divider (per-spot) vs gate (fixed 72 deg)
constants.documentedValue: gate fixed 72 deg vertical under `?fov=legacy`; divider per-spot fov measured 88.5 deg on serenity's eight 16:9 landscape spots, 120 deg on `10`/`11`, 65 deg on `9.webp`'s own `vfov` override
constants.documentedAt: CLAUDE.md:102 (pitch row, 'Two different cameras read this key' clause)
constants.measuredValue: Reproduced independently this session. Gate: tour/app.js:149 constructs the camera at fov=72; tour/measure.js:74-75 skips `__spotFov` entirely when `?fov=legacy` is present, leaving that 72 default in place. Divider: tour/main.js:120-130 `__spotFov(spot, aspect)` -- if `spot.vfov` is a positive number it is returned directly (9.webp: vfov=65, confirmed in tour/apartments/serenity.json); otherwise for aspect>=1 (landscape) it computes `2*atan(tan(photoFovLong/2 deg)/aspect)/1deg` with photoFovLong=120 (both apartments' meta.photoFovLong), which for aspect=16/9=1.7778 evaluates to 88.507 deg; for aspect<1 (portrait) it returns photoFovLong directly = 120 deg. Cross-checked against the REAL photo files with PIL: serenity's 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8.webp are all 1200x675 (aspect 1.7778, landscape) -> 88.5 deg; 10.webp is 923x1200 (aspect 0.769, portrait) -> 120 deg; 11.webp is 812x1200 (aspect 0.677, portrait) -> 120 deg; 9.webp is 919x1200 but carries its own vfov:65 override so the aspect is irrelevant.
constants.howMeasured: Read tour/main.js, tour/measure.js, tour/app.js source directly; independently recomputed the __spotFov formula in Python against real photo pixel dimensions (PIL) rather than trusting the prior citation
